meaning: Cool beans, slang for “wonderful,” expresses excitement or approval, often with a deliberately folksy tone.
example: So much homework to do this is not cool beans
origin_usage: Because it sounds like dated 1960–70s slang, cool beans may be used ironically, sometimes targeted at someone seen as uncool or older.

meaning: If someone is badd, they aren’t actually bad, they’re so cool that they’re great.
example: It's crazy how now-a-days a girl would rather be called sexy or badd rather than beautiful or gorgeous..
origin_usage: Badd is most often used in an overtly sexual context today. Whether it’s B.A.D.D. Magazine releasing its summer badd girls calendar of “Beautiful Ambitious Distinctive Divas” (adult film stars and models) or a social-media user posting a provocative selfie, being badd is about being unabashedly sexy.

meaning: A baller can refer to a great basketball player or a lavishly successful person. It can also describe someone or something as “excellent,” especially in some spectacular way.
example: That's Mitch being a baller and trying to make a play ... I'm excited for his future because he's a baller.
origin_usage: Baller is predominantly used in the worlds of sports and hip-hop, but it has spread into the culture at large, used as a noun and modifier for something or someone flashy, skilled, or exceptional.

meaning: Chef’s kiss is a gesture and expression meant to show something is perfect or excellent.
example: The new volume indicator alone is—chef's kiss—a feature iOS has needed for years. And iMessage search, well, it's downright amazing.
origin_usage: Online, people may write chef’s kiss—often in asterisks as *chef’s kiss* to represent an action being performed—in reaction to something they find simply exquisite in some way. Its tone can be sincere.

meaning: Something described as picture perfect is considered flawless or ideal in appearance or character.
example: The game has one of the most memorable art styles in years and turns every moment into a picture-perfect display of cartoon merriment.
origin_usage: The phrase picture perfect can be used by anyone to describe anything that is flawless or, more loosely, is beautiful or high-quality. Picture perfect is especially said of physical appearances, marriages, families, homes, and vacations.

meaning: A power couple is a romantic or married couple where both members are famous or accomplished in their own right. The term is sometimes extended to happy and productive everyday couples.
example: The power couple rocking their fashion on a magazine cover. You love to see it.
origin_usage: Power couple is often seen in the popular press and social media, especially entertainment news and gossip. While the sense of power couple has broadened, celebrity power couples continue to be an object of fascination.

meaning: A rainbow baby is a baby that is born after a miscarriage, stillbirth, or loss of an infant.
example: The baby is worth it. I had a miscarriage a little over a year ago & I’m currently pregnant with my rainbow baby. I also have Hyperemesis Gravidarum. It’s been ROUGH so far. But I know it’ll be worth it in the end to hold my baby.
origin_usage: Rainbow baby is an affectionate and loving term used by parents, especially mothers, in discussions of pregnancy or child loss. Parents like to photograph their newborn rainbow babies in rainbow colors. Keep in mind, though, that the topic, and therefore the term, can be very sensitive and personal.

meaning: Spooning is a form of cuddling where two people lay on their sides, with one person’s back against the other’s chest. In this position, the two people resemble two spoons nested together in a drawer.
example: Why do guys always want to be the little spoon while spooning
origin_usage: Cuddlers talk of spooning. It’s commonly discussed in relationship columns and lifestyle publications, whether how to spoon so your arm doesn’t fall asleep or how to spoon so you can snooze all night long.

meaning: Tendies is a slang term referring to gains or profits made on investments, such as stocks.
example: The Hedge fund owners tears will season our tendies. Hold the line.
origin_usage: The usage of tendies spread to a joke about how profits would be spent to a way to refer to the profits themselves. Eventually, tendies gained wider attention and more mainstream use due to the forum’s role in a widely discussed situation involving investment in what became known as meme stocks.

meaning: Word up is a slang phrase used to show agreement, approval, or excitement.
example: Never be the one with the most to say and the least to offer. Word up!
origin_usage: Word up is used on social media to express agreement, excitement, or approval.

meaning: An almond mom is a parent who follows incredibly strict or dangerously unhealthy eating habits and attempts to force them on their children.
example: The worst part about growing up with an almond mom is that now that I’m an adult, I can buy all the cool kid unhealthy stuff for myself but I’m too old to truly enjoy it
origin_usage: Almond mom is used to refer to parents that have unhealthy, strict diets that they force on their children.

meaning: Awkward turtle is often said humorously in uncomfortable situations, especially for endearing or cutesy effect.
example: I can talk so easy over social media and then I’m an awkward turtle in person.
origin_usage: A person who feels awkward themselves or who has observed something they find embarrassing may issue an awkward turtle as mild, humorous social commentary. Someone might also be called an awkward turtle if they are seen as quirky or clumsy. This is usually not done in a mean way, but rather in a loving, playful way—an embrace of nerd-dom and imperfection.

meaning: Usually butterface is used for a woman whose body is attractive but whose face is ugly.
example: Sorry but the gym can’t fix that butterface.
origin_usage: Butterface is a mashup of the pronunciation of the phrase “but her face.” The term is based on a sexist joke about women’s appearances. For example, a man might remark after a blind date that “everything about her was attractive but her face.”

meaning: A concern troll offers undermining criticisms under the guise of concern. Their goal is to sabotage the cause being discussed, and to inspire doubt among group members.
example: “Was a little surprised this afternoon by a concern troll advocating the need for more fat shaming in order to 'save the children'. Huh.”
origin_usage: A concern troll will make statements with the intent to cause discord in a community, while pretending they’re doing it out of concern for the greater movement. Concern trolling is a lot like playing devil’s advocate in online debates, but as a tactic to infiltrate movements or causes and weaken them.

meaning: Hamster angle is a novelty term for when a selfie makes your face look chubby, like a hamster’s.
example: And there I was, I accidentally called her and she saw me from a really chubby hamster angle
origin_usage: Hamster angle is mainly a novelty term, seeing only occasional use for selfies. The concept of the hamster angle implies it is undesirable, but some people may think it’s cute.

meaning: A problem child is a child who is considered difficult. The term is also used as a metaphor for a persistently trying or demanding person, thing, or responsibility.
example: After two days of discussion at the 3rd Mexico Infrastructure Projects Forum in Monterrey, Mexico, the role of natural gas has emerged as a bit of a problem child, albeit an important part of the nation's ongoing energy reforms.
origin_usage: Problem children is commonly used to compare and contrast an unruly child with their siblings.

meaning: A problematic fave is a character or person who’s done or said offensive (i.e. problematic) things.
example: “No matter what happens…Mick Rory will always be my fave. Problematic fave yes. But definitely fave (after Leonard of course)”
origin_usage: The phrase problematic fave encourages fans of a person to critically consider that person’s words and actions. On the blog, “Your fave is problematic,” each entry begins in this way: “Your fave is problematic: [person’s name].” This format spreads knowledge of these actions and encourages critical discussion of their issues.

meaning: Sadfishing is the act of posting about your emotional problems online for attention or personal gain.
example: Sadfishing: my male colleagues are laughing at my work related questions and make me feel bad about myself
origin_usage: Sadfishing is based on catfishing, which is a slang term for the act of deceiving or swindling someone by assuming a false identity online.

meaning: Shadow banning is a practice used in online moderation that consists of preventing a user’s content from being seen by others—either partially or totally—without the user being notified or aware of it.
origin_usage: The word ban is commonly used as both a noun and verb in the context of online moderation, typically used in situations in which a user’s access to a platform is permanently blocked. The word shadow is used in a similar way in other terms that imply a sense of stealth or secrecy.

meaning: Throwing shade is a subtle way of disrespecting or ridiculing someone verbally or nonverbally.
example: We could be untouchable as a group if we spent less time bickering & throwing shade and more working and planning towards projects to better those around us.
origin_usage: Throwing shade enjoys broad use in colloquial speech and digital communication. The phrase is especially used in internet memes to make light of petty feuds between celebrities, politicians, and other public figures. It is often discussed alongside side eye. One preferred method of throwing shade is via “subtweets” on Twitter. Subtweeting involves subtly criticizing someone without referring to them directly or tagging their username.

meaning: Adorkable is an informal adjective used to describe someone as being cute or likable due in part to having characteristics considered “dorky,” such as being a bit awkward or having unusual interests.
example: I absolutely love this scene when Tony and Peter Parker first meet. Great comedic timing and Tom Holland was adorkable. #CaptainAmericaCivilWar
origin_usage: Adorkable is always used positively by people who intend it as a compliment.

meaning: A dayt is a romantic date that occurs during the daytime.
example: anyone wanna go on a dayt with me
origin_usage: Dayt is an informal, largely playful term associated with the millennial generation. It is occasionally used to communicate expectations for a slow or platonic relationship or outing or about the person on that outing or in that relationship.

meaning: People who are egotastic believe the world revolves all around them, and they’re not afraid to be showy about it.
example: You're so egotastic. I wanna slap you with a newly served sunny side egg
origin_usage: Egotastic can be a more light-hearted, enthusiastic way to describe extraordinarily egotistical behavior.

meaning: Friyay is a slang term used as an informal synonym for Friday. It’s also used as an interjection to celebrate and express joy that it’s Friday (and thus the beginning of the weekend), very similar to how the term TGIF is used.
example: HAPPY FRIYAY!!! What're you doing this weekend?!
origin_usage: Friyay is primarily used on social media by people celebrating the arrival of Friday. It’s commonly used as an informal synonym for Friday, as a celebratory interjection, or as the hashtag #Friyay.

meaning: Observed on February 13, the day before Valentine’s Day, Galentine’s Day celebrates platonic friendships, usually among women.
example: happy galentine's day to the amazing and strong women in my life thx for being such wonderful inspirations to better myself every day ily
origin_usage: While Galentine’s Day is more popular among women, the holiday itself can also include, as long as the relationship is non-romantic, male and other nonbinary friends.

meaning: Realest is the superlative form of real, used in slang for someone or something “extremely authentic” or “exceptional.”
example: I feel i'm the realest friend a person can have. If you don't know anything know ima ride til the wheels fall off baby
origin_usage: Realest is particularly present in black speech and on social media. In this slang meaning, someone who is the realest is the “best” in that they are original and down-to-earth—always, sometimes vulnerably, true to who they are and treating others the same way. Referring to someone as the realest is a sign of respect for their consistent dedication, talent, loyalty, or other positive qualities. In this way, realest is generalizing as a slang term for “excellent.”

meaning: A person is sliving when they are glamorously successful, self-empowered, and fulfilled—they are “killing it” all on their own, loving every minute of it, and lookin’ good while doing it.
example: I just made a lasagna following Paris Hilton’s famous recipe! Loves it! @ParisHilton #Sliving #CookingWithParis
origin_usage: Paris Hilton loves to use sliving in the media and online (as the hashtag #sliving), especially when she is doing something particularly glamorous, fun, or great in some way. In interviews, Hilton often plays with grammatical forms of the word, e.g., I slive, I am sliving, you are a sliver.

meaning: Smexy is a blend of smart and sexy, referring to someone who has both brains and beauty.
example: Smexy group of men. (Thanks for that massive tricep to lean on, Mustaga)
origin_usage: Smexy is used as a cutesy way to call a person both good-looking and intelligent. It’s especially used of men by women on the internet.

meaning: To smize is to smile with your eyes, usually in a sexy and playful way.
example: Good morning. Now get out there and SMIZE at a stranger!
origin_usage: According to Tyra Banks, former model and host of America’s Next Top Model, to smize is to “smile with your eyes,” blending the word smile with the sound of the word eyes, hence the spelling smize.

meaning: A quirkyalone is a person who prefers being single to being in relationship with someone just to be in one.
example: Singlehood is now being celebrated as a legitimate lifestyle; we’re called “proud singles” or “quirkyalones.”
origin_usage: Quirkyalone was coined by writer Sasha Cagen. As she defines a quirkyalone: “A person who enjoys being single (but is not opposed to being in a relationship) and generally prefers to be alone rather than date for the sake of being in a couple.” She also uses it as an adjective to describe the quirkyalone behavior of such people. Use of quirky suggests that preferring singleness is eccentric or anomalous in the eyes of mainstream culture but also that quirkyalone individuals embrace that identity.

meaning: Brigading is a slang term for an online practice in which people band together to perform a coordinated action, especially a negative one, such as manipulating a vote or poll or harassing a specific person or members of an online community.
example: If you’ve never been a victim of online “brigading,” let me tell you right now - it’s scary, it’s overwhelming, and it’s exhausting.
origin_usage: The term brigading is typically used in a critical way by those discussing coordinated actions online, especially ones considered to be forms of harassment or manipulation of polls or voting. The verb form of the term is also used.

meaning: The term coronaversary is a slang term with several meanings, all related to the COVID-19 pandemic. It can refer to a wedding anniversary that occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic, the anniversary of the start of the COVID-19 outbreak, or the anniversary of the beginning of COVID-19 lockdowns. Coronaversary is often used in a facetious or ironic tone to express frustration with the various challenges caused by COVID-19.
example: It’s almost our one year coronaversary, one year down, hopefully no more to go
origin_usage: The term coronaversary is used on social media to mark the anniversary of the COVID-19 virus outbreak or to celebrate a wedding anniversary that happened during the pandemic. The former uses are usually meant to be sarcastic or flippant.

meaning: An edgelord is someone on an internet forum who deliberately talks about controversial, offensive, taboo, or nihilistic subjects in order to shock other users in an effort to appear cool, or edgy.
example: I can't stand people who try and act smart by being entirely pessimistic. Like grow up, edgelord.
origin_usage: Especially on social media sites, edgelord is used to insult people who think they are being cool by being especially risqué, provocative, or dark. Edgy, if you will. Usually, though, they just end up sounding offensive.

meaning: Feminazi is an offensive slur for a feminist whose views are considered radical or extreme.
example: The feminazis just didn’t like human nature. They thought it was unkind to them, for one thing, and they just didn’t like it.
origin_usage: Feminazi is a sexist slur used in speech and digital communication. It seeks to discredit feminists by portraying them as extreme.

meaning: Referring to the act of lowering your forehead to your desk, headdesk is an expression of extreme frustration, aggravation, or resignation.
example: Remember when AMERICAN HUSTLE wasn't even nominated for an Oscar for Best Makeup and Hairstyling? *headdesk*
origin_usage: If you are faced with something so incredibly frustrating that a facepalm isn’t enough, it’s time for a headdesk.

meaning: Maskne is acne or other skin irritation that results from wearing a mask, especially a medical, N95, or cloth face mask.
example: Is anyone else getting this maskne or is it just me. My face is breaking out horribly.
origin_usage: Currently, maskne almost exclusively refers to facial acne and other skin irritation on the face caused by frequently wearing masks during the COVID-19 pandemic.

meaning: Demotional is a slang coinage meaning “detached and emotional” for those who is really passionate yet doesn’t let things get under his skin.
example: I used to be detached before, Then I become emotional, Now I am Demotional.
origin_usage: The word demotional is intimately associated with Shah Rukh Khan. SRK uses it of himself, and his fans and Bollywood reporters use it of his personal life and acting. Khan, an acclaimed actor, is obviously a very expressive person capable of great emotion. However, he’s said he’s learned to steel himself against bad reviews and harsh criticisms of his films—he’s detached, aloof, dispassionate, but still gets a lot out of life.

meaning: Selfiecide is the act of accidentally dying while trying to snap that perfect selfie.
example: Please do not commit selfiecide.
origin_usage: While that photo of you swimming next to a shark might get some serious likes, you, unfortunately, won’t be around to enjoy them. It appears our obsession with praise, validation, and self-presentation has literally gotten the better of us.

meaning: Unalive is a slang term used on social media as a replacement for the verb kill or other death-related terms, often in the context of suicide.
example: my mom will unalive me if she ever sees my sketchbook help
origin_usage: Unalive is most commonly used by younger social media users as a way of avoiding platform restrictions around use of terms related to killing and suicide. It is used in both serious and nonserious ways.

meaning: Whitesplaining is the act of a white person explaining topics to people of color, often in an obliviously condescending manner, and especially regarding race- or injustice-related issues.
example: the other tried to whitesplain to me that "there are bigger issues for Natives to worry about other than mascots," to which I promptly told him that he doesn't get to decide which Native issues are more important, among other things.
origin_usage: Whitesplain and whitesplaining are commonly used in the context of white people trying to talk about issues people of color face (e.g., racism and marginalization) to other people of color.

meaning: Alpha refers to a dominant person or their behavior, especially with respect to socially aggressive, hyper-masculine men.
example: All of that Messi hype and it's Marcos Rojo who rescued Argentina. Alpha male.
origin_usage: As a description for a man, alpha became a term sometimes embraced and aspired to and other times challenged. Meanwhile in the 2000s, alpha female emerged as a positive term for powerful, successful women, though not without intimidating plenty men.

meaning: Drip means that your look or style is extremely fashionable or sexy.
example: I was gonna call a plumber till I realized it’s my sauce that’s dripping
origin_usage: Thanks to Cardi B, drip often appears in the phrase come through dripping, e.g., I came through drippin’ tonight with my red bottoms. This phrase is a favorite of people posting outfit pics on Instagram and Twitter when they feel especially have the drip or are dripping in designer goods.

meaning: Not many people can claim to be the G.O.A.T., but those who can are the Greatest Of All Time in their field. Most often, the acronym G.O.A.T. praises exceptional athletes but also musicians and other public figures.
example: today marks the 10th anniversary since the release of Lil' Kim's debut mixtape "Ms. G.O.A.T."! for killerbees, it's not just a record, it's a celebration of female rap unity & Kim's brilliance. with this tape, the queen taught us how to respect other ladies in the game. HPB!
origin_usage: G.O.A.T. is a fun one, usually said and even written just like the simple word goat.

meaning: One has juice if they have respect, influence, power, authority, or sexual desirability.
example: at some point in your life, you have to stop hanging with people who got the tea and establish yourself with ppl who got the juice
origin_usage: In contemporary black slang, juice, perhaps influenced by its historical sexual and power connotations, is slang for qualities like credibility, clout, having the respect of one’s peers, and being sexually desirable. It is often used in the context of someone having (or not) the juice.

meaning: Pick six is an informal term used in American football to refer to an interception (informally called a pick) that’s returned for a touchdown (which is worth six points). In other words, it’s a name for what happens when a defensive player intercepts a pass and is then able to return the ball all the way to the opponent’s end zone, thus scoring a touchdown.
example: Ohio State cornerback Denzel Burke said his 23-yard interception return for a touchdown against Rutgers today was his first pick-six ever as a football player.
origin_usage: Pick six is informal, but it’s the most common way of referring to an interception returned for a touchdown. It’s considered among the most exciting plays in football.

meaning: Woke means being conscious of racial discrimination in society and other forms of oppression and injustice.
example: Fake woke locals tweeting “stop joking about XXX death” whilst tweeting “can Taylor Swift die” are we surprised?
origin_usage: As a result of its mainstream appropriation, woke toggles between several uses. It is still used for awareness of and activism against forms of oppression and injustice. It is also used for being conscious of “true reality” more generally, of not accepting conventional wisdom. Artificial intelligence, for instance, is often described as woke when it becomes self-aware. Woke is also sometimes just used to characterize someone as “hip” or “open-minded” as well as the source of plenty of cute puns. Finally, in Black English, woke can also still mean just being literally “awake,” harkening back to its roots.

meaning: Going platinum is a music industry term used to describe a single or album that sells one million copies or more. If something has gone platinum, it’s extremely successful, or a smash hit.
example: Y’ALL SAY CONGRATULATIONS TO MY BROTHER @pstmn301 FOR GOING PLATINUM ON ‘EVERYBODY’. LOVE YOU DAWG CONGRATS!
origin_usage: In the record industry, going platinum is a term that holds a real numerical value, and it’s used officially by artists, media, and others to describe successful single and album sales that exceed 1,000,000 units.

meaning: Hugs and kisses is an expression of love, physical and emotional affection, and well wishes
example: I'm your Mister, you my Misses with hugs and kisses / Valentine cards and birthday wishes, please
origin_usage: In speech contexts, you may encounter hugs and kisses when a parent, grandparent, long-time partner, or, in some instances, a very close friend is saying a goodbye. It’s often used when one person is sending along their love to a person (or pet) they aren’t directly speaking with.

meaning: Featured in the video game Dark Souls, Praise the Sun is an expression of relief, delight, or gratitude, often used humorously and accompanied with uplifted arms.
example: “Class cancelled three times this week praise the sun”
origin_usage: Praise the Sun has the quality of interjections like thank God. It’s used to convey gratitude, joy, or relief for something good that’s happened. It can also be used sarcastically or with a sense of ironic resignation or despair in the face of intractable problems.

meaning: Relationship goals characterize various actions, or couples themselves, that display a depth of connection someone wants in their own love life.
example: Some lady told my aunt she hated her so my uncle shook up a beer and sprayed it in her face #RelationshipGoals
origin_usage: Many people use relationship goals to signal what they earnestly hope for in a couple or to celebrate a couple who has achieved great happiness in love.

meaning: An hero is used by the dark parts of the internet as a mocking synonym for the act of suicide or for someone who has died by suicide.
example: The suicide ... gave name to a whole new concept, 'an hero' to describe sensational media suicides.
origin_usage: An hero is used primarily as a synonym for suicide and is often “suggested” as a good idea for users with bad opinions or users who’ve embarrassed themselves, similar to Kill Yourself.

meaning: Beta is a slang insult for or describing a man who is seen as passive, subservient, weak, and effeminate.
example: Companies would much rather hire skinny beta male dorks than an attractive alpha type. Less competition for the females at the firm. Natural
origin_usage: More stereotypically macho men use beta to insult men they see as weak or passive.

meaning: A brick wall is variously used as a metaphor for a challenging obstacle or obstruction.
example: I hate when you’re talking to someone and you feel like you’re talking to a brick wall because they just do not care or can’t take 2 mins to listen to what you are saying
origin_usage: Brick wall is extensively used in speech and writing in a range of metaphorical constructions. As noted, some authors and editors may look down upon uses of brick wall as clichés in formal writing. We may say we hit a brick wall when we’ve run out of money or energy for a project. Or, if a loved one isn’t acknowledging our feelings, we may say it’s like talking to a brick wall. In these uses, brick wall may not indicate final defeat but rather extreme frustration or exasperation. To see through a brick wall is “to be especially perceptive” and to run through a brick wall is “to be extremely powerful or rebellious.”

meaning: Mid is a slang term used to describe something or someone as mediocre or of low quality.
example: If you don't have that t.i , fab, or yo gotti mixtapes....your playlist is mid
origin_usage: The slang term mid seems to have emerged as a shortening of the word middle. The term mid is typically used to humorously insult someone or something as bad or inferior in some way, especially when regarded as excellent or high quality by others.

meaning: Shook is the past tense form of shake, used as a slang term to describe feelings ranging from discombobulation and fear to rage and elation, kind of like “all shaken up.”
example: Y’all ever just get shook at your own beauty ? Because same
origin_usage: Shook often comes up when describing extreme emotions set off by a sexy person or violent situation. On the internet, the slang shook is used for more hyperbolic or ironic states of fluster, such as the charm of a cute boy or cute dog.

meaning: Snowflake is a political insult for someone who is perceived as too sensitive, often used for millennials and liberals.
example: This liberal snowflakes are too damaged for adulthood / *curls into a ball at the thought of a transgender fighter pilot*
origin_usage: Truer to its Fight Club origins, snowflake is often used by “back in my day” folks to criticize millennials and Generation Z for being coddled, whiny, and in need of kid-gloves treatment.

meaning: Sportsball is a mildly critical or humorous term used by people who admit they don’t know or care about sports.
example: Sportsball is back. I’m single again.
origin_usage: Sportsball is mostly used in a lightly mocking or judgmental way by people who proudly don’t like or know anything about sports. It can also knock people seen as way too fanatical about sports or to characterize sports as a waste of time.

meaning: This guy is an expression used to highlight when someone has done something stupid or unbelievable. It’s often used to reference oneself.
example: Whose got two thumbs, two straps, and a twitch channel? This guy. | stream schedule: 915am est, 3pm est MUSIC!
origin_usage: Get a load of this guy is often used to taunt someone seen as stupid, ridiculous, or, occasionally, striking in some way.

meaning: A person has too much sauce when they wear too many designer clothes and accessories at the same time and, by extension, when they display the (over)confidence such items might afford them.
example: ‘Do Better’ has just too much sauce in one song.
origin_usage: Too much sauce is often used by young people, particularly young black people, to compliment confident, talented, or attractive people or things in the same way bad is used to mean “good.”

meaning: Someone’s who’s washed (out) might be burnt out, exhausted, or, if they’re a drug user, extremely high.
example: I know im washed because i watch Good Mythical Morning everyday while smoking a blunt
origin_usage: The word washed has been around since Old English, and it literally means “cleaned.” By the 1790s, the expression washed out was in use, referring to clothes that had been washed so many times their color had faded. By the early 20th century, both washed up and washed out had taken on figurative meanings. In 1923, the expression washed up meant “no longer effective.” This sense comes from washing up after finishing a job. Over time, washed up referred to someone who’d fallen out of popularity, particularly a performing artist. Washed out similarly took on a figurative sense for someone who is exhausted or out of energy.
